title: Bringing the Strands Together
summary: Students run one guided challenge through all four strands and explain how each link in the chain shaped the next.
objectives: Complete a guided challenge combining the concept, a prompted solution, an output check and a risk check.
Explain how the system type and prompt shaped the output.

body: This term you learned four skills one at a time. Today you discover they were never separate - they form one chain, from understanding the system to writing a prompt, checking the output, and using it responsibly. Put all four hats on at once.

sections.heading: I can…
items: I can complete a guided challenge that uses all four strands.
I can explain how the system type and prompt shaped the output.
I can name one responsible-use choice I made.

terms.definition: Connecting separate skills into one process.
Whether a system is rule-based or learning-based.
The instruction you give an AI tool to guide its output.
Judging an output as correct, incorrect, or unclear.
Asking what could go wrong and choosing a responsible action.

sections.heading: One connected chain
body: The [[system type]] shapes what you can expect. The [[prompt]] shapes the output. The output needs a [[triage]]. And the whole process needs a [[risk check]].
Each strand feeds the next - miss one link and the chain weakens.

sections.label: The whole term in one line
sections.heading: Four skills, one chain
sections.altText: A chain of four steps: work out the system type, write a structured prompt, triage the output, then run a risk check.

edges.label: so you know what to expect
so the output is worth judging
so you know what you are risking

sections.caption: Each step only makes sense because of the one before it. **Skip the first and you do not know what the tool was ever going to be able to do.**

sections.heading: Explain the links
body: It is not enough to complete each step; you should be able to explain how one shaped the next.
For example: because the prompt was specific, the output stayed on task, which made triage easier and the risk lower.

sections.label: Let's try it - hands-on
sections.heading: Let's try it - hands-on
body: Run one guided challenge through all four strands, then explain how the system and prompt shaped the output and name one responsible-use choice you made.
items: Name the system type behind the task.
Write or choose a clear prompt.
Run a basic risk check and note a responsible-use choice.
Explain how the system and prompt shaped the output.

sections.heading: Think about it
items: Which strand was strongest in your work, and which needs practice?
How would a weaker prompt have changed the whole chain?

sections.heading: My reflection
items: Write which strand you will focus on before the signature solution.
Explain one link in the chain in your own words.

worksheet.title: Week 6 - Core - Worksheet | Bringing the Strands Together

questions.prompt: Complete each of the four steps for the guided challenge.
questions.stem:
System type:
My prompt:
Triage verdict and reason:
Risk check and choice:
questions.lookFor: All four steps recorded: a named system type (e.g. a learning system for a text summariser, contrasted with rule-based), a specific prompt, a triage verdict of correct / incorrect / unclear with a checkable reason, and a genuine risk-reduction choice such as keeping personal data out of the prompt.

questions.prompt: Write two sentences linking system, prompt, and output.
questions.stem:
Because the system was ...
The prompt made the output ... which means ...
questions.lookFor: Both stems completed so that system and prompt are clearly linked to the output - e.g. a specific prompt gave a focused, on-task summary while a vague one would drift. Approaching links only two strands; not yet treats the strands as separate.

questions.prompt: Record your result for each strand.
questions.stem: Strand | What I did | Result | Link to next strand
questions.lookFor: One row per strand with the action taken, a result, and a link showing how each strand fed the next: system type shapes the prompt, the prompt shapes the output, the output demands a triage, and the whole process demands a responsible-use choice.

questions.prompt: Explain how the system type and prompt shaped your output, and name one responsible-use choice you made.
questions.lookFor: Connects system plus prompt to the output quality and names a genuine risk-reduction choice that was made during the task (e.g. no personal data in the prompt), not added afterwards.

questions.prompt: Redesign the prompt to lower the risk further, and predict how the output and triage would change.
questions.lookFor: Redesigned prompt targets the risk that was identified (e.g. removes personal data, asks for checkable statements) and the prediction explains how both the output and the risk would change - the stretch expectation for this lesson.

formative.targets: Integrates all Term-1 Emerging outcomes before the signature solution
formative.check: Guided integration task reviewed against project success criteria; forward feedback
formative.successCriteria: Connects system+prompt to output, triages the output, and names a risk-reduction choice.
